content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 18-19. This unit focuses on consistency, transactions, and events.

Information and concurrency concerns meet where systems update data over time. Transactions, event streams, eventual consistency, idempotency, and compensating actions all express architectural choices about correctness and coordination.
The architect should decide which operations require strong consistency, which can tolerate delay, and how users and operators will observe or repair inconsistent states.
Studio: pick three operations in an ecommerce system and classify each as strong consistency, eventual consistency, or compensating workflow.

concepts.name: Data consistency
concepts.description: The degree to which data remains correct and aligned across operations, stores, and system boundaries.

concepts.name: Eventual consistency
concepts.description: A consistency model where replicas or dependent systems converge after a delay rather than immediately.

concepts.name: Idempotency
concepts.description: The property that repeating an operation has the same effect as performing it once.

concepts.name: Compensating action
concepts.description: A corrective operation used to undo or offset effects when a distributed workflow cannot use a single transaction.
